claims.text: Thousands of US military members have lived aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln for more than 250 days.
Lawmakers are demanding answers from the Pentagon over reported food shortages, broken plumbing, and exhaustion aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.
Military news outlets reported that some sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have attempted to jump overboard.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth called reports of poor conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln 'completely misrepresented'.
The USS Abraham Lincoln departed California in November for the South China Sea before being redirected to the Middle East ahead of attacks on Iran in February.

Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal wrote a letter to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth detailing reported supply shortages, water contamination, and deteriorating mental health aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.
Arizona Senator Ruben Gallego requested that a bipartisan congressional delegation be allowed to visit the USS Abraham Lincoln to conduct an oversight investigation.
CBS News reported that a sailor went overboard from the USS Abraham Lincoln in early August, was rescued by helicopter, treated, and transferred off the ship.
A relative of a sailor aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln stated that the sailor had lost 29kg (65lbs) since beginning deployment.
A US Navy official told the BBC that traditional supply hubs were disrupted by combat actions in the region.
The USS Abraham Lincoln originally departed San Diego on November 21 and arrived in the Middle East in January ahead of the US-Israel conflict with Iran that began on February 28.
The aircraft carrier USS George Washington is travelling toward the Indian Ocean to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East.
Senator Richard Blumenthal gave Pentagon leadership a deadline of August 27 to respond to six questions regarding Navy fatigue and morale tracking.
Annabelle Loma told the Navy Times that her husband, who is serving on the USS Abraham Lincoln, attempted to go overboard during his deployment.
Around 200 relatives confronted acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao and senior commanders during a meeting in San Diego regarding the extended deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln.
The USS Abraham Lincoln made a brief port call in Oman in early July, where crew members stocked up on fresh produce while restricted to a secure compound.
US President Donald Trump claimed online that the US Navy has 'total control' over the Strait of Hormuz.
Israeli forces instructed residents of approximately a dozen Palestinian households in Qusra to leave their properties during an operation to remove Israeli settlers.
Israeli settlers besieged three Palestinian homes in Qusra starting on Sunday, cutting off power and water supplies.
Israeli spokesman David Mencer called the settlers' siege in Qusra 'deplorable' and 'unacceptable'.
The Israel Defense Forces stated they dismantled two illegal outposts and detained one Israeli near Qusra and Jalud.
US Ambassador Mike Huckabee described the settler intimidation of Palestinian families in Qusra as a 'horrific act of terror'.
Israeli forces ordered Palestinian families in Qusra to evacuate their homes and took up positions inside the properties.
Maj Gen Avi Bluth visited Qusra on Wednesday and committed to evacuating Israeli settlers from the village.
Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert described the siege of Qusra as a 'concerted and meticulous attempt at ethnic cleansing'.
Israeli civilians and soldiers have killed more than 1,100 Palestinians in the occupied West Bank since 2020, resulting in one indictment.
One of the three besieged homes in Qusra is owned by Loui Ridi, a Palestinian-American citizen who resides in Ohio.
The UN Human Rights Office in the occupied Palestinian territory urged Israeli authorities to act immediately against the settlers in Qusra.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum stated that Colombia refused entry to a Mexican military rescue team by requesting additional certification.
Colombia accepted 58.5 tonnes of aid from Mexico following Monday's earthquake.
Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella announced that Colombia will receive a $10m donation from the United Arab Emirates.
A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck western Colombia shortly after 7:30am local time on Monday.
Colombian authorities reported on Thursday that more than 150 aftershocks occurred following the main earthquake.
The epicenter of Colombia's magnitude 7.4 earthquake was located in the Choco region near San Jose del Palmar at a depth of 100 kilometers.
An earthquake double-event in Venezuela on June 24 killed more than 6,300 people in 2026.
Government figures indicate that at least 273 people were killed, at least 3,800 injured, and 377 listed as missing following the earthquake in Colombia.
Approximately 50 percent of the University Hospital of the Valle Evaristo Garcia in Cali was structurally damaged by the earthquake.
Cali city authorities declared a 'red alert for hospitals' as public hospital capacity reached 100 percent on Monday.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that Polish authorities thwarted a Russian plot to kill a Ukrainian-American citizen in Warsaw.
Polish authorities arrested the suspect accused of planning the assassination in Warsaw on August 7.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that this was the first known instance of someone acting on Russian orders attempting to attack a US citizen on NATO territory.
Polish security minister Tomasz Siemoniak confirmed that the arrest of the Russian suspect was carried out in cooperation with US services.
Russian caricaturist and Putin critic Semyon Skrepetsky was shot dead in eastern Poland in June.
A fleet of 15 boats evacuated over 250 tourists and locals from the beach at Siviri, Greece, as a wildfire approached homes.
The UK recorded a provisional temperature of 38.1C at Kew Gardens in London, making it the country's hottest day of 2026 so far.
The Royal College of Nursing stated that nurses collapsed from heat exhaustion while working in UK hospitals lacking adequate air conditioning.
Southern Water applied for a drought order in Britain that could restrict non-essential water usage.
Dutch bank Triodos estimated that extreme heatwaves and drought could reduce EU gross domestic product by 1 percent in 2026, or around €180 billion.
Romania shut down the second of two nuclear reactors at its only nuclear power plant due to record-low water flows on the Danube River.
German public health officials estimated that 12,500 people died from heat-related causes during the summer.
Russian President Vladimir Putin made his first visit to the Kuril Islands, stopping on Iturup.
Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi strongly protested Putin's trip to Iturup and summoned Russian Ambassador Nikolay Nozdrev.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi condemned Putin's visit as 'absolutely unacceptable' and incompatible with Japan's position on the Northern Territories.
Russia has strengthened its military presence on the Kuril Islands by deploying Bastion coastal defence missile systems and Su-35 fighter aircraft.
Approximately 17,000 Japanese residents formerly lived on the Kuril Islands before being deported by the Soviet Union, and around 20,000 Russian citizens live there now.
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo spread to a sixth province following a death in Bas-Uele.
Government figures show the current DRC Ebola outbreak has killed 2,128 people out of 4,566 confirmed cases.
Mercy Corps warned that confirmed Ebola cases sit 35 kilometres from the South Sudan border.
The current Ebola outbreak in DRC is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, which lacks approved vaccines or treatments.
Health workers at the Nizi Treatment Center in Ituri province went on strike over unpaid salaries for three months, temporarily closing the facility.
Genetic sequencing showed that the Ebola outbreak in DRC began in February, months before its official declaration on May 15.
The World Bank estimates that 70 percent of the population in Zambia survives on less than three dollars a day.
Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema is seeking a second term against the Tonse Alliance led by Brian Mundubile.
Former Zambian President Edgar Lungu died in South Africa in June 2025.
Annual inflation in Zambia fell to 6.5%, down from 24.6% in July 2021.
Parliament's Monsoon session ended with Lok Sabha productivity at 19% and Rajya Sabha productivity at 39%.
Parliament passed 12 bills during the Monsoon session, including the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill.
The Lok Sabha completed zero Question Hours during the 25-day Monsoon session due to daily disruptions.
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister following student protests over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.
The Lok Sabha referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill to a 31-member joint parliamentary committee.
Police identified the suspect who attacked Sukhbir Singh Badal as 62-year-old Jaspal Singh Teja Singh Aidal, a law graduate from Pune.
Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal suffered injuries to his arm and shoulder in a kirpan attack outside Gurdwara Mata Sahib in Nanded.
Sukhbir Singh Badal previously survived an assassination attempt at the Golden Temple in Amritsar on December 4, 2024.
At least six workers died and 14 were injured when water and debris flooded an under-construction hydroelectric tunnel in Pipalkoti, Chamoli.
The flooded tunnel in Chamoli is a 2km-long Tail Race Tunnel constructed by Hindustan Construction Company for THDC.
A Bailey Bridge at Tamak Nala in Chamoli was swept away by surging water on August 10.
The Bar Council of India reversed its directive blocking NALSAR's 2026 graduating batch from advocate enrolment, allowing students to seek enrolment.
The BCI gave NALSAR three days to submit an authenticated report identifying individuals who organised the campaign against Chief Justice Surya Kant.
Approximately 450 out of roughly 1,400 NALSAR students supported the objection to inviting Chief Justice Surya Kant to the convocation.
Abhijeet Dipke founded the Cockroach Janta Party after Chief Justice Surya Kant referred to youth as 'cockroaches' during a court hearing in May.
